title: Repair a comma splice with a shared subject
instructions: Choose the revision that forms one complete sentence without changing the meaning.

parts.prompt: Original: “Rina finished the safety checklist, she handed it to the coordinator.” Which revision is correct?

options.text: Rina finished the safety checklist and handed it to the coordinator.
Rina finished the safety checklist, she handed it to the coordinator.
Because Rina finished the safety checklist and handed it to the coordinator.
Rina finished the safety checklist. And handed it to the coordinator.

choice_rationales.A: The two actions share the subject Rina, so and can join the verb phrases without repeating the subject.
choice_rationales.B: A comma alone cannot join the two independent clauses.
choice_rationales.C: Because makes the whole wording dependent and leaves no main clause.
choice_rationales.D: The words after the full stop have no stated subject and form a fragment in this context.

parts.hint: Both actions are performed by Rina. Join the two verb phrases under their shared subject.
parts.correct_explanation: The revision uses one subject, Rina, with the coordinated verb phrases finished and handed.
